events.title: The death of Pope St. John Paul II
events.shortBlurb: After twenty-six years on the Chair of Peter, the pilgrim pope died as the vigil of Divine Mercy Sunday began…
body: Pope John Paul II died at 9:37 in the evening of 2 April 2005, in his private apartment in the Apostolic Palace, aged eighty-four, as the vigil of Divine Mercy Sunday — a feast he himself had established in 2000 — was beginning. Born Karol Wojtyła at Wadowice in Poland in 1920, he had been elected on 16 October 1978, the first Polish pope and the first non-Italian in 455 years.

His reign of twenty-six and a half years was among the longest in the Church's history, exceeded only by those of Peter and Pius IX. It gave the Church the Catechism of 1992, fourteen encyclicals, an unprecedented number of beatifications and canonizations, and more than a hundred journeys abroad, while his moral witness played its part in the peaceful collapse of communism in eastern Europe.

His last years, borne openly with Parkinson's disease, were themselves a teaching on suffering. Some four million mourners came to Rome for his funeral on 8 April, where the cry of 'Santo subito' — sainthood now — rose from the square. He was beatified in 2011 and canonized, together with John XXIII, on 27 April 2014.

sources.text: Vatican biography, St. John Paul II (vatican.va)
